Answer: B
Reason: Visual inspection of Figure 1 reveals a curvilinear opacity (indicated by the arrow) descending along the right heart border, which is the characteristic "scimitar sign" of anomalous pulmonary venous return; additionally, the right hemidiaphragm appears elevated relative to the left, consistent with the hypoplasia often associated with Scimitar syndrome. Although the report generator failed to identify these specific features due to limitations, direct visual verification confirms the classic radiographic presentation described in option B.
